author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T070125Z-233736
text:
Escalating after initial scoping pass. Two architectural questions need maintainer call before implementation:

(1) **Discovery only vs discovery + chain validation.** The bead's acceptance says 'cRLSign + chain-to-anchor checks performed on discovered signer.' But pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:123-126 (current rustdoc Limitations) explicitly says: 'The cRLIssuer's chain is NOT validated by this crate — callers must present an already-validated cRLIssuer cert. Composing this with pkix-path to validate the cRLIssuer chain in-process is the umbrella crate's responsibility (pkix-chain).'

That stance is consistent with AGENTS.md non-neg #2 (chain → revocation → path: revocation does not pull in chain validation). Two reasonable resolutions:

 - **Option A (discovery only):** pkix-revocation walks bundle, matches AKI→SKI, verifies cRLSign bit. Assumes bundle contents are pre-validated. pkix-chain composes this with its own path validation when it builds the CrlChecker. Architecturally consistent. Smaller change.
 - **Option B (discovery + chain):** pkix-revocation invokes pkix_path::validate_path on the discovered signer with the caller-supplied trust anchors. Changes the trait surface (CrlChecker now needs anchors). Architecturally inverts the rustdoc comment above. Bigger change.

(2) **Constructor surface.** Three plausible API shapes:

 - **New constructor on CrlChecker:** CrlChecker::new_with_signer_discovery(crl_der, bundle: &[Certificate], now_unix, verifier) -> Result<Self>. Mirrors new_with_crl_issuer; discovery happens at construction time and the result is stored as crl_issuer_cert. Plus a delta variant.
 - **New wrapper type:** struct BundleCrlChecker<V> wrapping CrlChecker<V> + bundle; check_revocation does discovery per call. More expensive at check time but cleaner separation.
 - **Trait helper free fn:** discover_crl_signer(bundle, &crl) -> Option<&Certificate>; caller still constructs CrlChecker via new_with_crl_issuer. Most explicit, least magical. Easiest to compose at higher layers.

Recommend (1)=A, (2)=trait helper + new constructor variant on CrlChecker.

Rationale for (1)=A: preserves the existing one-way dep, keeps pkix-revocation lean. pkix-chain already exists to compose path + revocation, so layering discovery+chain there is natural. Also, the PKITS workaround in pkix-revocation/tests/pkits_4_5.rs:22-29 explicitly notes that the existing API checks (a) issuer.subject == CRL.issuer, (b) cRLSign on issuer, (c) CRL signature against issuer.SPKI — i.e., the caller-presents-validated-signer pattern is already the de-facto contract. Adding discovery to the same crate without adding chain validation honors that contract.

Rationale for (2)=helper + constructor: a free fn discover_crl_signer keeps the AKI/SKI walk testable in isolation and reusable by pkix-chain at compose time. A matching CrlChecker::new_with_signer_discovery constructor provides one-call ergonomics for callers that have a flat bundle and don't want to compose manually.

Acceptance criterion 4 ('PKITS §4.5 and §4.14 tests run without the mechanical workaround') would still be met under (A+helper+constructor): the workaround in tests/pkits_4_5.rs:20-29 (manual AKI→SKI walk) gets replaced by either calling the helper directly or by using the new constructor.

If maintainer endorses (A) + the helper+constructor pair, this bead is implementable in roughly: ~150 LOC new code (helper + constructor + bundle-walk logic), rustdoc, ~6-8 tests covering §4.5 and §4.14 PKITS chains, and removal of the workaround in tests/pkits_4_5.rs. The §6.3.3(f) text in the bead is naturally interpreted as 'pkix-revocation does cRLSign + AKI-matching; pkix-chain ensures the bundle was chain-validated' rather than 'pkix-revocation does both.'

Leaving open and unclaimed pending maintainer call on (1) and (2).
